# mobile-glb-budget

Purpose: Set explicit triangle / texture / draw-call / file-size / animation budgets for GLB targeted at mobile-web before any export decision.

Translate "make it work on mobile" intent into a concrete numeric planning ceiling table (triangles, vertices, GLB file size, texture pixels, materials, draw calls, animation channels, bones, morph targets) per device tier, scene scope, and target context. Pin this budget before scene mutation so downstream scene planners consume it, `polycount-budget-checker` and `material-quality-checker` validate counts and textures against it, `render-export-evidence` measures compliance, `glb-web-handoff` consumes it for web delivery, and `glb-animation-handoff` owns animation contracts.

Metadata: Contract `v1.0.0` | Category `evidence-and-handoff` | Role `mobile-webgl-budget-validator` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- before scene plan is locked
- before any GLB export attempt
- when user says "for mobile" / "for the web" / "phone" / "low-end devices"
- when designing a scene that must run alongside other web content
- Trigger phrases: "what's a good polycount for mobile", "how big can the GLB be", "will this load on iPhone", "what should I aim for on a phone"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- desktop-only renders without web handoff → use `polycount-budget-checker` (`references/skill-polycount-budget-checker.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to polycount-budget-checker)
- offline pre-rendered video (no real-time budget needed) → use `material-quality-checker` (`references/skill-material-quality-checker.md`; no real-time budget needed)
- replacing engineering load testing (this skill sets a planning budget, not a real-world benchmark) → use `glb-web-handoff` (`references/skill-glb-web-handoff.md`; this skill sets a planning budget, not a real-world benchmark)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `target_device_tier_and_network` (`string`): Target mobile/web hardware tier (iOS Safari, mid-range Android, desktop WebGL) and load budget
- Required input `scene_deliverable_type` (`string`): Whether the GLB is a single hero product, multi-item configurator, or animated character
- Optional input `compression_pipeline_support` (`object`): Whether the host app supports Draco, Meshopt, or KTX2 BasisU transcoding
- Output contract: `pinned_glb_performance_budget_table`, `triangle_drawcall_and_texture_ceilings`, `compression_and_lod_requirements` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Quick-start steps
1. pick the device tier (low-end Android, mid-mobile, high-mobile, desktop-fallback)
2. read the budget row for that tier
3. pin the budget into the scene plan before mutation
4. treat any later violation as a blocker, not a warning

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: BlendOps runtime guidance uses **2 MCP execution paths plus a CLI fallback appendix** (see `docs/runtime-stack-strategy.md`):
- Run a real-world benchmark.
- Install Blender.
- Run Blender.
- Choose a render engine.
- Write web-side optimization code.
